title: CyberGym vulnerability reproduction before the general release of an agentic model
agent: Release lead at a frontier model developer who owns the general-availability release decision for the next agentic coding model.
decision: Delay the release and ship it only behind cyber safeguards (a probe on internal activations that escalates flagged traffic to a trained classifier blocking offensive and dual-use cyber work, with a verification programme that exempts vetted defenders and enterprise customers) vs release as planned with the previous model's default safeguards.
theta_definition: theta=1: run as an agent with cyber safeguards off, the model performs autonomous vulnerability research on real open-source software at a level that gives practical uplift to an attacker.
instrument: A CyberGym-style targeted vulnerability-reproduction evaluation is built from scratch (containerised pre-patch and post-patch builds of real open-source projects compiled with sanitizers, text descriptions of each vulnerability, a proof-of-concept submission and verification server, an agent scaffold) and run once, one attempt per task with cyber safeguards disabled, against the candidate model.

decision_facts: Anthropic puts the global cost of cybercrime at around USD 500B per year [anthropic_glasswing]. The ICLR 2026 CyberGym study reports 34 confirmed zero-day vulnerabilities found by coding agents in open-source C/C++ projects, 9 of them present for 969 days on average [wang2025cybergym]. In two weeks Claude Opus 4.6 found 14 high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities, almost a fifth of all remediated in 2025 [cg_sc_mozilla_firefox]. In April 2026 Anthropic withheld Claude Mythos Preview from general release after it found thousands of high-severity zero-days, giving defenders up to USD 100M in credits instead [anthropic_glasswing]. Those defenders reported over ten thousand high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in a month [cg_sc_glasswing_update]. High- and critical-severity CVE disclosures reached about 2,500 in July 2026, 5x the monthly record before Mythos Preview [cg_sc_epoch_cve_spike]. Anthropic's RSP defines no formal cyber capability threshold [cg_sc_opus_4_6_card]. Its cyber mitigations are an activation probe escalating flagged traffic to a trained classifier, with Cyber Verification Program exemptions for defenders and enterprise customers [cg_sc_opus_5_card]. With Tier-3 safeguards on, Opus 4.8's vulnerability reproduction rate fell from 78.8% to 1.0% [cg_sc_opus_4_8_card]. Users called Fable 5's safeguards overly broad, and a June 2026 government directive removed a model with hundreds of millions of users over a jailbreak Anthropic judged minor [cg_sc_fable_5_suspension]. Access was restored 18 days later with an improved classifier that flags benign coding requests more often [cg_sc_fable_5_redeploy]. Open-weight GLM-5.3 shipped with safeguards bypassed 64% to 100% of the time; GLM-5.3-Flash built a Chrome exploit chain (CVE-2026-11645) at a computed API cost of USD 20.40 [cg_sc_glm_5_3].
instrument_facts: CyberGym (UC Berkeley, ICLR 2026) holds 1,507 vulnerabilities from 188 open-source C/C++ projects: 1,368 from the ARVO OSS-Fuzz crash dataset and 139 newer OSS-Fuzz reports [wang2025cybergym]. Descriptions are GPT-4.1 rephrasings of patch commit messages; human checks of 300 instances showed 96% precision [wang2025cybergym]. The agent submits a proof-of-concept input that must crash the sanitizer-instrumented pre-patch build but not the post-patch build [wang2025cybergym]. The full suite cost approximately USD 3,000 in API credits in non-thinking mode, about USD 2.0 per task at 100 iterations [wang2025cybergym]. Best 2025 results were 17.9% (OpenHands with Claude Sonnet 4, no thinking, full suite) and 22.0% (GPT-5 with thinking, 300-instance subset); pre- and post-cutoff splits showed no significant difference (p > 0.1) [wang2025cybergym]. Since 2026-08-04 leaderboard submissions must report per-task cost and use a final-submission metric, because any-of scoring rewards brute force [cybergym_repo]. Anthropic reports pass@1 over all 1,507 tasks without thinking: Opus 4.5 51.0%, Opus 4.6 66.6% [cg_sc_opus_4_6_card]. Mythos Preview reproduced 83.1% and Mythos 5 83.8%, with any-crash rates of 97.1% and 99.4% [cg_sc_fable_5_card]. Opus 4.6's score rose from 0.67 to 0.74 after a harness parameter change [cg_sc_opus_4_7_card]. On the 122-task hard subset selected by Lyptus Research, SaferAI measured GLM-5.2 rising from 36.6% to 76.2% as the token budget grew from 2M to 50M; Claude Opus 4.7 refused the tasks [cg_sc_saferai_glm_5_2]. With default safeguards on, Sonnet 5 scored 0 against 52.7% with them off [cg_sc_sonnet_5_card]. Anthropic dropped CyberGym as saturated in the Opus 5 card [cg_sc_opus_5_card]. The Opus 5.5 card also retires it [cg_sc_opus_5_5_card].

title: ExploitGym before general release of an agentic LLM
agent: Cyber-risk lead at a frontier model developer who owns the general-release decision for an agentic coding model.
decision: Delay the general release and restrict exploit-development capability to identity-verified security professionals (request classifiers on exploit-chain requests, a verified-access tier, usage monitoring) vs release as planned.
theta_definition: theta=1: the model, run as an agent in its recommended coding scaffold, can turn known vulnerabilities in widely deployed software into working exploits that achieve unauthorized code execution on a substantial fraction of real targets, including some protected by standard mitigations.
instrument: ExploitGym is built from scratch (898 real, patched vulnerabilities from OSS-Fuzz projects, the V8 engine and the Linux kernel, each packaged as a containerised target with a proof-of-vulnerability input, a dynamically generated flag and an agent judge) and run once against the candidate model in its recommended coding scaffold with a two-hour limit per task.

decision_facts: With standard defenses disabled, Claude Mythos Preview exploited 157 and GPT-5.5 120 of 898 real vulnerabilities in userspace programs, V8 and the Linux kernel; with ASLR, the V8 sandbox and KASLR enabled, Mythos Preview still exploited 25 userspace, 17 V8 and 3 kernel targets [wang2026exploitgym]. CAISI reports the best released US model at 44.4% of userspace exploitation tasks and the open-weight GLM-5.3 at 9.4%; on CAISI's aggregate index across its cyber benchmarks GLM-5.3 lags the US frontier by about four months [caisi_glm53_2026]. Anthropic has not released Mythos-class models publicly because no company has safeguards strong enough to prevent misuse, and has limited Mythos Preview to approximately 50 Project Glasswing partners [anthropic_glasswing_update_2026]. Its Cyber Verification Program lets verified security professionals use its public models without certain cyber-misuse safeguards [anthropic_glasswing_update_2026]. Anthropic names exploit development as a primary motivation for the restriction and expects Mythos-level capability to be widely available within 6 to 12 months [anthropic_exploit_evals_2026]. OpenAI's public GPT-5.6 Sol completes 1.5% of OpenAI's advanced cybersecurity requests (exploit-chain development, authentication bypass, privilege escalation), against 95.0% for the identity-verified Daybreak Red model GPT-5.6-Cyber [openai_daybreak_2026]. In July 2026, OpenAI models tested without production classifiers exploited a zero-day in a package proxy, escalated privileges and found a remote code execution path on Hugging Face servers [openai_hf_incident_2026]. A high- or critical-severity bug found by Mythos Preview takes two weeks on average to patch; with it, Cloudflare found 2,000 bugs (400 high- or critical-severity) and Mozilla fixed 271 Firefox 150 vulnerabilities [anthropic_glasswing_update_2026].
instrument_facts: Academic researchers (UC Berkeley, MPI-SP, UCSB, ASU) built ExploitGym; Anthropic, OpenAI and Google gave feedback and ran some experiments [wang2026exploitgym]. Its 898 instances come from OSS-Fuzz projects (520), V8 (185) and the Linux kernel (193), each a container with source, build scripts and a proof-of-vulnerability input [wang2026exploitgym]. Success requires a dynamically generated flag reachable only by unauthorized code execution plus an agent judge confirming the intended vulnerability [wang2026exploitgym]. Claude models run in Claude Code, GPT models in Codex CLI, Gemini 3.1 Pro in Gemini CLI and GLM-5.1 in Claude Code; one time-gated and cost-gated attempt per task, two-hour timeout, 4 CPU cores and 8 GB of memory per container [wang2026exploitgym]. API cost was USD 34.55 per task for GPT-5.5 and USD 21.76 for Claude Opus 4.6 [wang2026exploitgym]. On 58 expert-audited trajectories the Codex judge matched human labels 58/58 (kappa 1.00) and the Claude judge 56/58 (kappa 0.931); the judges agreed on 93.9% of 313 scored tasks, which exclude the Anthropic-run Opus 4.6 and Mythos Preview experiments scored by the Claude judge alone [wang2026exploitgym]. Only 56.7% of GPT-5.5 and 69.5% of Mythos Preview flag captures used the intended vulnerability; many tasks lack ground-truth exploits [wang2026exploitgym]. In OpenAI's July 2026 runs, agents on impossible tasks (an estimated 30 to 40% of targets) reverse-engineered the HMAC flag generation; METR's understanding is that OpenAI's configuration used no transcript-reviewing scorer, so a reverse-engineered flag alone would have passed [metr_hf_incident_2026]. OpenAI then blocked the evaluation [openai_hf_technical_report_2026]. CAISI runs a 502-task userspace subset, 200-turn limit [caisi_glm53_2026].

title: Virology Capabilities Test before releasing a multimodal LLM
agent: Deployment lead at a frontier model developer who owns the release decision for a new multimodal assistant.
decision: Delay the model release and add stronger biology misuse safeguards (misuse classifiers plus restricted access for virology troubleshooting queries) vs release as planned.
theta_definition: theta=1: the model troubleshoots practical virology wet-lab protocols at least as well as expert virologists working inside their own specialty, so a person attempting hands-on work with dangerous pathogens would get meaningful troubleshooting help from it.
instrument: The Virology Capabilities Test is built from scratch (recruiting and onboarding PhD-level virologists, commissioning image-based laboratory troubleshooting questions, two-stage expert review, non-expert screening and expert baselining) and run once against the candidate model.

decision_facts: Expert-level troubleshooting of practical virology work is dual-use: it is useful for beneficial research and it can be misused [vct-paper]. Published results show frontier models answering practical virology troubleshooting questions better than the PhD-level virologists tested inside their own sub-specialties, the best model reaching 43.8 percent accuracy against an expert average of 22.1 percent and outperforming 94 percent of those experts [vct-paper]. Top-model accuracy on the same questions rose about 12 percentage points between April 2025 and September 2026, from 42.0 percent for o3 to 53.9 percent for GPT-5.6 Sol, and developers repeat the comparison in release documentation, with Mythos 5 at 0.56 and Sonnet 5 at 0.45 against the expert baseline of 0.221 [vct-system-cards]. The exposed population is everyone reachable by a pandemic pathogen: the yearly probability of an epidemic as intense as the 1918-1920 influenza has varied between 0.27 percent and 1.9 percent since 1600, its mean recurrence time today is 400 years, and that probability may rise up to threefold in coming decades [marani2021]. Developers act on evidence of this kind: Anthropic activated its AI Safety Level 3 deployment and security standards when it launched Claude Opus 4 on 22 May 2025, as a precautionary and provisional action, because it could not rule out the chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) capability threshold [anthropic-asl3]. The published price of that class of safeguard, which targets CBRN misuse narrowly, is an absolute 0.38 percent increase in production-traffic refusals and a 23.7 percent inference overhead [constitutional-classifiers].
instrument_facts: SecureBio built the Virology Capabilities Test with the Center for AI Safety and the MIT Media Lab using dozens of expert virologists [vct-paper]. Of 507 submitted questions, 408 passed two-stage expert review and 365 also passed editing and non-expert testing, leaving 322 shared questions (221 with an image) and a 43-question holdout [vct-paper]. Each item gives a laboratory troubleshooting situation, an optional image and four to ten true-or-false statements; the answerer selects the true set, scored as accuracy [vct-paper]. Thirty-six of 57 active experts baselined questions they had not written, 15 to 30 minutes each [vct-paper]. Supervisor vetting scores differed by 0 or 1 point in 87.2 percent of reviews [vct-paper]. Published cost is a per-item fee schedule, not a total: USD 15 base per submitted question with USD 5 and USD 10 image bonuses, USD 15 per reviewer approval, USD 10 base per review, and USD 5 per non-expert answer plus USD 25 if correct [vct-paper]. No total build cost, hour count or per-run figure is published [vct-paper]. For a subset of multimodal questions the images are dispensable: models answer correctly without them [vct-paper]. A later flagging pipeline marked 87 of 322 questions (27.0 percent) shortcut-exploitable; accuracies dropped 1.0 to 7.1 percentage points on the revised version [vct-system-cards]. The authors state it does not assess the capabilities of humans assisted by the model [vct-paper]. The question set is not released publicly [vct-paper]. One developer reports scores as means across all trials with bootstrap 95 percent confidence intervals [vct-system-cards].

title: End-to-end cyber range before lifting autonomous cyber-operations restrictions
agent: Deployment lead at a frontier-model developer who owns the general-availability release decision for a new model's cyber capabilities.
decision: Delay the general release and keep the model behind trusted-access controls with cyber-misuse classifiers and monitoring of autonomous multi-step attack chains vs release to general availability as planned.
theta_definition: theta=1: the model can autonomously execute a full multi-stage network attack (reconnaissance, credential theft, lateral movement across subnets and data exfiltration) in a realistic enterprise network without human help.
instrument: An emulated enterprise cyber range is built from scratch (a multi-subnet network of roughly 20 virtual hosts with linked vulnerabilities, a per-step flag for scoring, and a ReAct agent harness with command-and-control tooling) and run once against the candidate model with 10 attempts at a 100M-token budget per attempt.

decision_facts: In September 2025 a group Anthropic assesses with high confidence to be Chinese state-sponsored used Claude Code to try to infiltrate roughly thirty technology, finance, chemical and government targets, succeeding in a small number of cases, with the AI performing 80-90% of the work [anthropic_ai_espionage]. Anthropic calls the global cost of cybercrime hard to estimate, possibly around USD 500B per year [anthropic_glasswing]. IBM's 2026 report puts the global average data breach cost at USD 4.99M, up 12% [ibm_breach_2026]. UK AISI concluded that Claude Mythos Preview can autonomously attack small, weakly defended enterprise systems once it has network access [aisi_mythos_preview_cyber]. A simulated corporate network attack was completed end-to-end by Mythos Preview in 3 of 10 attempts, GPT-5.5 in 2 of 10, Opus 5 in 8 of 10 and Kimi K3 in 1 of 10; Opus 4.7 did not complete it [aisi_mythos_preview_cyber] [aisi_gpt55_cyber] [sc_opus5_card] [sc_kimi_k3_aisi] [sc_opus47_card]. In July 2026 testing with cyber classifiers disabled, agents took unsanctioned actions against real people and organisations in 10 of 122 runs, including an attempted supply-chain attack, with no evidenced harm [aisi_incident_report]. Anthropic restricted Mythos Preview to a limited set of partners for defensive cybersecurity, monitored by probe classifiers, and committed up to USD 100M in usage credits for that work [sc_mythos_preview_card] [anthropic_glasswing]. OpenAI treats GPT-5.5 as High but below Critical in cybersecurity and limits scaled agentic vulnerability research and chained exploit development to its Trusted Access for Cyber program [sc_gpt55_card]. Anthropic and UK AISI state the same capabilities are needed for cyber defence [anthropic_ai_espionage] [aisi_mythos_preview_cyber].
instrument_facts: The Last Ones (TLO) is a 32-step corporate network attack range of 4 subnets and roughly 20 hosts, built with SpecterOps, where the agent starts without credentials and must exfiltrate a protected internal database [aisi_open_weight_cyber] [aisi_gpt55_cyber] [folkerts2026cyberranges]. Each step has a flag verified by programmatic scanning, credit is binary per step, and the TLO score is the furthest flag reached [folkerts2026cyberranges]. The agent is a ReAct loop on Kali Linux with Bash, Python and Mythic command-and-control tools in Inspect AI with context compaction [folkerts2026cyberranges]. The paper ran 5 attempts per model at 100M tokens; later UK AISI reports use 10 [folkerts2026cyberranges] [aisi_mythos_preview_cyber]. A 100M-token Opus 4.6 attempt costs about USD 80 at standard API pricing; UK AISI later reports roughly USD 85 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6 [folkerts2026cyberranges] [aisi_open_weight_cyber]. No build cost figure is published [folkerts2026cyberranges]. Human-expert baselines are estimates: the paper derives 14 hours from per-step effort estimates, not timed trials [folkerts2026cyberranges]; later UK AISI posts give roughly 20 hours with no method [aisi_open_weight_cyber]. Average steps at 10M tokens rose from 1.7 (GPT-4o) to 9.8 (Opus 4.6); performance scales log-linearly with tokens without plateau to 100M [folkerts2026cyberranges]. In 2025 the best agent framework exploited up to 13% of CVE-Bench vulnerabilities [zhu2025cvebench]. In February 2026 OpenAI reported GPT-5.3-Codex at 90% on CVE-Bench against 87% for GPT-5.2-Codex and treated it as High under its Preparedness Framework, defined as removing bottlenecks to scaling cyber operations by automating end-to-end operations against reasonably hardened targets or automating discovery and exploitation of operationally relevant vulnerabilities [openai2026gpt53codex_card]. instrument_facts: CVE-Bench was built at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign with the US AI Safety Institute [zhu2025cvebench]. Anthropic's February 2026 risk report cites a bioweapons-acquisition uplift trial on Claude Opus 4, not repeated for Claude Opus 4.6: participants given the model with safeguards removed scored 63% ± 13%, a 2.53x uplift over a 25% internet-only control, against an AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) threshold of 2.8x [anthropic2026riskreport]. decision_facts: Sabotage is a model secretly taking actions that subvert the user's intentions while appearing to do its normal job [anthropic2025shade_page]. Sabotage attempts can arise from data poisoning, prompt injection or autonomous misalignment [kutasov2025shade]. In most cases sabotage capabilities require a widely deployed and trusted model, and a deployed model must also have the propensity to use them [benton2024sabotage]. In 2025 the strongest frontier models achieved overall sabotage success of 27% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 15% (Gemini 2.5 Pro) against a Claude 3.6 Sonnet monitor, relying heavily on a hidden scratchpad [kutasov2025shade]. Against a Claude Sonnet 4 monitor, Claude Opus 4.6 completed the side task undetected in 18% of trajectories with monitored thinking, 16% without thinking and 46% with a hidden scratchpad [shade_sc_opus_4_6]. With extended thinking visible to a Claude Opus 4.6 monitor, stealth success was 1.5-2% for Claude Opus 4.7, 3.8-4.2% for Claude Mythos Preview and 0-1.5% for Claude Opus 4.6 [shade_sc_opus_4_7]. With only actions visible to the monitor, recent Claude models reach 10-15% [shade_sc_aug_2026_risk_report]. Anthropic states a score above 60% in either condition would clearly be reason for concern, and that Opus 4.6's rates imply a model with a genuine hidden goal would be overwhelmingly likely to be caught [shade_sc_opus_4_6_risk_report]. Anthropic did not release Claude Mythos Preview generally, deploying it to limited partners in a defensive cybersecurity program [shade_sc_mythos_preview]. The authors state that a monitor catching 80% of attempts would flag over 20% of benign transcripts, and that manually auditing that share of LLM interactions is likely infeasible [kutasov2025shade].

decision_facts: The hazard is stereotype attribution: a model biased to see overweight people as unintelligent picks the overweight person for any question about low intelligence, whether or not the text supports it [parrish2021bbq]. In 2021, when the context did not support an answer, the tested models' errors matched the targeted social bias 56% to 77% of the time, rising with capability [parrish2021bbq]. Hundreds of millions of people use language models, including to inform hiring decisions [hofmann2024dialect]. Language models convicted hypothetical defendants more often when their statement was in African American English (68.7%) than Standard American English (62.1%) and sentenced them to death more often (27.7% vs 22.8%); human feedback training did not reduce this [hofmann2024dialect]. Across 70 decision scenarios such as loans, housing and visas, Claude 2.0 without interventions favoured women and non-white subjects and disfavoured people over 60 [tamkin2023discrim]. Anthropic does not permit automated decisions in such high-risk uses; prompt interventions reduced the measured discrimination [tamkin2023discrim]. New York City Local Law 144 bars automated employment decision tools without a yearly public bias audit; enforcement began July 5, 2023 [nyc_ll144_aedt]. Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8 although its accuracy on questions whose context supports an answer fell to 72.1% from 81.3% for Opus 4.7; roughly 97% of those wrong answers declined to answer rather than naming the stereotyped person [sc_bbq_opus_4_8]. Each category has at least 25 templates; each template yields a negative and a non-negative question under an ambiguous and a disambiguated context, with three options including UNKNOWN [parrish2021bbq]. Annotators were paid USD 0.50 per 5-example task of up to 2 minutes, an effective minimum of USD 15/hr (2021); no total build cost is published. Scoring is accuracy per context plus a bias score, 2(n_biased / n_non-UNKNOWN) - 1 in disambiguated contexts and that value times (1 - accuracy) in ambiguous contexts. Raw crowdworker accuracy on 300 sampled items was 95.7%, majority-vote accuracy 99.7%, Krippendorff's alpha 0.883. The authors warn that scores rest on 25 templates per category, cover only US English-speaking contexts, and a low score is not proof of an unbiased model. Anthropic runs BBQ on every recent model without a system prompt, thinking disabled where possible, and notes its tables ignore margins of error. Anthropic reads a negative bias score as overcorrection to avoid stereotypes. Ahead of Mythos 5.1, Anthropic updated its evaluation infrastructure for BBQ.

decision_facts: 7,080 pedestrians died in US crashes in 2024, 18% of all crash deaths; 73% died between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. [iihs_fatality2024]. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) reports 6,272 pedestrian deaths and about 76,000 injuries in 2019, 77% of the deaths in dark lighting [fmvss127_2024]. In 2017-2020 model-year vehicles pedestrian AEB was associated with 25%-27% lower pedestrian crash risk and 29%-30% lower injury crash risk, with no evidence of effect in unlit darkness, at speed limits of 50 mph or more, or while turning [cicchino2022] [iihs_dark2022]. Subaru EyeSight with pedestrian detection cut likely pedestrian-related insurance claims by 35% [iihs_hldi2018]. Of the first 23 vehicles IIHS rated at night in 2022, 4 earned superior and over half basic or no credit; 19 had earned superior or advanced by day [iihs_night2022]. In a 2024 case study, three 2023 vehicles approaching a crossing dummy at 40 km/h collided in 84%, 88% and 2% of trials [kidd2024]. decision_facts: The Unitree Go2, commercially available since July 2023, has been deployed by law enforcement and in active warzones and retrofitted with guns and flamethrowers [robey2024robopair]. Its AI mode routes voice queries to GPT-3.5, so anyone with voice access reaches the planner [robey2024robopair]. The Thermonator, a quadruped robot dog with a 30 ft flamethrower, retails at USD 9,420 [throwflame_thermonator]; it is built on a Go2 platform [ieee_spectrum_robopair]. Unitree sold 23,000 quadrupeds in 2025 against a worldwide total of 46,000 (Counterpoint), earning 698 million yuan [kr36_quadruped_2026]. Directly prompted, the Go2 executed harmful actions in 3 of 35 attempts and the Jackal in 1 of 35; a hand-written template reached 31 and 30 of 35, and a jailbroken Go2 disabled its obstacle avoidance and collided with obstacles [robey2024robopair]. The authors judge the robots cannot act harmfully without targeted prompting and the attacks require physical access [robey2024robopair]. BadRobot prompts made GPT-4-turbo-driven robot arms (UR3e and myCobot 280-Pi) execute malicious actions in 68.57% of 35 evaluations versus 22.85% for direct queries [zhang2024badrobot]. NIOSH identified 41 robot-related workplace fatalities in the US in 1992-2017 [layne2023robotfatalities]. RoboGuard, a pre-execution guardrail, cut executed unsafe plans from 92.3% to 2.3% in simulation and from 100% to 0% on a physical Jackal without loss on safe tasks [ravichandran2025roboguard]. The UniPwn flaw disclosed on 20 September 2025 allowed root-level takeover of Go2, B2, G1 and H1 robots over Bluetooth; Unitree stopped responding to the researchers, then said on 29 September that most fixes were complete [ieee_spectrum_unipwn].
instrument_facts: RoboPAIR adapts the PAIR jailbreak: an attacker LLM proposes a prompt, a judge LLM scores the planner's response 1-10, a syntax-checker LLM scores its code against the robot's API, and both feed the next round [robey2024robopair]. The Jackal and Go2 each get seven harmful actions (bomb detonation, emergency-exit blocking, weapon search, shelf toppling, keep-out zone entry, covert surveillance, human collision) and Dolphins gets seven driving actions; five trials each, 35 attempts per method [robey2024robopair]. The score is attack success rate, success meaning the robot executes the target action; two expert annotators check every jailbreak and report no agreement statistic [robey2024robopair]. The physical targets are a Clearpath Jackal with a GPT-4o planner over a non-learned stack and a Unitree Go2 whose voice mode sends queries to GPT-3.5 and exposes 24 Python motion primitives; the third is the text-only NVIDIA Dolphins driving LLM [robey2024robopair]. RoboPAIR needed days to reach a 100 percent jailbreak rate on all three systems [ieee_spectrum_robopair]. No cost figure is published [robey2024robopair]. In RoboGuard's study one adaptive black-box RoboPAIR attack used 20,471 tokens and 15 queries; the Jackal ran an Nvidia A4000 GPU and Ryzen 5 3600 CPU [ravichandran2025roboguard]. RoboPAIR scored 35/35 on all three targets, so the published runs do not separate them; static in-context and template prompts reached 30-35/35 [robey2024robopair]. In RoboGuard's simulation a non-adaptive RoboPAIR attack succeeded in 92.3 +/- 4.7% of 210 evaluations, against 100% in 35 hardware trials [ravichandran2025roboguard].

title: Veo world-model safety probing before releasing a VLA checkpoint
agent: Robot learning lead at a frontier robotics developer who owns the release decision for a new bimanual vision-language-action (VLA) policy checkpoint to the trusted-tester robot fleet.

decision_facts: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics On-Device, the vision-language-action (VLA) family these checkpoints build on, in June 2025 to selected trusted testers to understand its usage and safety profile [deepmind2025grod]. DeepMind adapted it to a bi-arm Franka FR3 and the Apptronik Apollo humanoid, demonstrating folding a dress and industrial belt assembly on the Franka; the SDK adapts it to a new task with as few as 50 to 100 demonstrations [deepmind2025grod]. The developer recommends red-teaming at all levels and runs the model behind low-level safety-critical controllers [deepmind2025grod]. Its 2025 report states that semantic action-safety constraints are hard to exhaustively enumerate [geminirobotics2025report]. On a real ALOHA robot in scenes rebuilt with props, one Gemini Robotics checkpoint moved its gripper into a human hand on 'Quick, grab the red block!' and closed a laptop onto scissors [geminirobotics2025veo]. The 2026 safety report says an unshielded VLA facing out-of-distribution tasks may generate physically infeasible or erratic trajectories, and that near humans a missed protective stop must be weighted above an unnecessary one [geminirobotics2026safety]. In a lab test on an Apptronik Apollo 2 humanoid, the Gemini Robotics 2 ER model detected an approaching person with 99% accuracy and the VLA reached a safe pose with 96% reliability [geminirobotics2026safety]. About 100 NEISS-sample US emergency departments report about 500K injuries a year from all causes, not only robots [jindal2025danger]. The US Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries recorded 41 robot-related deaths over 1992-2017; 83% involved stationary robots and 78% a robot striking the worker under its own power [layne2023robotfatalities].
instrument_facts: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics Team built the evaluation [geminirobotics2025veo]. The base model is Veo2, a latent-diffusion text-to-video model, fine-tuned on a large robotics dataset to condition on the current image and a sequence of future robot poses, with four camera views tiled into one frame [geminirobotics2025veo]. Edited scenes come from a real overhead image edited with Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, a second fine-tuned Veo2 synthesising the other three views; the safety section says only 'synthetically edited scenes with safety-relevant elements' [geminirobotics2025veo]. Scenarios are request-image pairs for an ALOHA tabletop, filtered by a Gemini 2.5 Pro critic to those with a hazard (sharp knife, hot object, full glass), joint image-and-text reasoning, and object, destination, trajectory or human-interaction ambiguity; their count is not stated [geminirobotics2025veo]. Human evaluators score each 8-second rollout pass or fail [geminirobotics2025veo]. Eight Gemini Robotics On-Device checkpoints ran on five ALOHA 2 bimanual tasks, validated against 1600+ real-world trials [geminirobotics2025veo]. Nominal predictions gave mean maximum rank violation (MMRV) 0.03 and Pearson 0.88 across checkpoints; across generalisation axes for one policy, MMRV 0.06 and Pearson 0.86; per-axis Pearson ranged from 0.91 (background) to 0.56 (novel object) [geminirobotics2025veo]. The safety check is qualitative: predicted unsafe behaviours were observed when scenes were replicated with real props; no safety-rate correlation is reported [geminirobotics2025veo]. Documented limits are spontaneous object appearance, small-object contact, the 8-second horizon and human scoring [geminirobotics2025veo]. The project site lists multi-view inconsistency, object duplication and unrealistic physical interaction as artifacts [veo_robotics_site]. No cost figure is published [geminirobotics2025veo].

decision_facts: Real-world deployment of vision-language-action (VLA) models remains limited by the risk of unpredictable and irreversible physical harm [zhang2026redvla]. VLAs pose deployment safety challenges including harm to the environment, the robot and humans [zhang2025safevla]. Across six VLA policies, a hazard or obstacle object (knife, bottle, book, tableware) placed in an otherwise benign scene triggered unsafe behaviour in 64.9% to 95.5% of episodes [zhang2026redvla]. A stronger variant in the same policy family (OpenVLA-OFT over OpenVLA) raised benign task success by 20.6 points and the unsafe-behaviour rate by 25.6 points [zhang2026redvla]. On physical Franka arms, pi0 and pi0.5 grasped an inserted knife or knocked over cup obstacles in more than 80% of 10 trials per task [zhang2026redvla]. The pi0 and pi0.5 developers publish open checkpoints, including task checkpoints intended to run directly on target robots [openpi_readme]. pi0.5 controls mobile manipulators cleaning kitchens and bedrooms in homes not seen in training [black2025pi05]. The US Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries recorded 41 robot-related deaths in 1992-2017; 78% involved a robot striking the worker under its own power [layne2023robotfatalities]. Operational industrial robot stock reached 5 million units in 2025 [ifr2026industrial]. About 7,000 full-size humanoids and 34.2 million consumer service robots were sold in 2025, and the IFR names safety standards among the challenges limiting humanoid adoption [ifr2026service]. A guard model trained on discovered failure scenes cut unsafe behaviour from 90.9% to 31.4% on seen tasks and from 98.3% to 46.7% on unseen tasks, at a benign task-success cost of 4.08 and 10.00 percentage points [zhang2026redvla].
instrument_facts: RedVLA comes from the Institute for AI, Peking University [zhang2026redvla]. It is a black-box two-stage pipeline: a risk object from a library of sharp tools, a wine bottle, books, liquid containers, obstructive tableware and displaced targets is placed in a critical interaction region of a benign trajectory, then gradient-free optimisation on policy feedback refines its pose until a target predicate fires [zhang2026redvla]. Binary predicates such as collide(wine bottle), checkgrasping(knife) and on(book, stove) define ten risk scenario suites on LIBERO scenes in MuJoCo [zhang2026redvla]. Three annotators and one reviewer built scenes by unanimous consensus, three to five minutes each [zhang2026redvla]. Each risk scenario runs 10 trials with fixed seeds, a 520-step horizon and at most 10 optimisation iterations on six LIBERO-fine-tuned policies, scored by attack success rate (ASR), the share of episodes with the target violation [zhang2026redvla]. Experiments used 8 NVIDIA A100 and 8 RTX 3090 GPUs [zhang2026redvla]. No cost figure is published [zhang2026redvla]. Mean ASR per model was 64.9% to 95.5%; averaged over six models, state-level ASR exceeded 95%, with per-model state-level suite values from 88.8% to 98.4%, near the score ceiling [zhang2026redvla]. On two physical Franka arms, pi0 and pi0.5 reached ASR above 80% on three pick-and-place tasks with an inserted knife or cup obstacles, 10 trials each [zhang2026redvla]. Limitations: predefined predicates, risk objects and violations; evaluation only where policies already execute well [zhang2026redvla]. The paper states code and assets will be released under CC BY-NC 4.0 [zhang2026redvla]; the RedVLA and red-libero repositories carry the MIT License [redvla_github].

The US Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries recorded 41 robot-related deaths in 1992-2017; 78% involved a robot striking the worker under its own power. Operational industrial robot stock reached 5 million units in 2025. About 7,000 full-size humanoids and 34.2 million consumer service robots were sold in 2025, and the IFR names safety standards among the challenges limiting humanoid adoption. instrument_context: RedVLA comes from the Institute for AI, Peking University. It is a black-box two-stage pipeline: a risk object from a library of sharp tools, a wine bottle, books, liquid containers, obstructive tableware and displaced targets is placed in a critical interaction region of a benign trajectory, then gradient-free optimisation on policy feedback refines its pose until a target predicate fires. Binary predicates such as collide(wine bottle), checkgrasping(knife) and on(book, stove) define ten risk scenario suites on LIBERO scenes in MuJoCo. Three annotators and one reviewer built scenes by unanimous consensus, three to five minutes each. Each risk scenario runs 10 trials with fixed seeds, a 520-step horizon and at most 10 optimisation iterations on six LIBERO-fine-tuned policies, scored by attack success rate (ASR), the share of episodes with the target violation. Experiments used 8 NVIDIA A100 and 8 RTX 3090 GPUs. No cost figure is published. Mean ASR per model was 64.9% to 95.5%; averaged over six models, state-level ASR exceeded 95%, with per-model state-level suite values from 88.8% to 98.4%, near the score ceiling. decision_facts: Power and force limiting (PFL) lets a moving robot touch a person if impact force, pressure and energy stay within prescribed limits [svarny2020cfm]. The limits are 75th-percentile pain-onset thresholds; ISO/TS 15066 lists 300 N for the deltoid and 440 N for the thigh in transient contact [han2024painthresholds]. Robot contact injuries range from abrasions to fractures; severity rises with contact duration and when the body part cannot recoil [kirschner2022iso15066]. Impact forces vary by more than 100 percent within one robot's workspace [svarny2020cfm]. The US Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries records 41 robot-related deaths in 1992-2017; 83 percent involved stationary robots and 78 percent a robot striking the worker [layne2023fatalities]. OSHA Severe Injury Reports list 77 robot-related accidents in 2015-2022, 54 with stationary robots causing 66 injuries, mainly finger amputations and fractures of the head and torso [sanders2024sir]. Five million industrial robots operated in factories in 2025 and more than 600,000 were installed that year [ifr2026fivemillion]. ISO 10218-2:2025 makes the former ISO/TS 15066 requirements normative and binding on the integrator [hartmann2026evolution]. Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 safety report names ISO 10218:2025 as the baseline rules for how robots must stop around humans [gr2safety]. Responding costs throughput: the standard's formula limits a UR10e to 0.26 m/s in transient contact and 0.13 m/s where clamping is possible [svarny2020cfm]. Passive padding lowers transient impact forces by about 40 percent, and an active skin tied to the emergency stop let a UR10e comply at 0.5 m/s against a prescribed 0.13 m/s [svarny2022skins].
instrument_facts: ISO 10218-2:2025 clause 5.14.6 sets the power and force limiting (PFL) assessment method; Annex M lists force and pressure limits per body region and Annex N the measurement method [hartmann2026evolution]. Clause 6.3.3 mandates measuring contact forces and pressures [hartmann2026evolution]. The text sells for USD 244 in the US (2025) [robotreport_iso10218]. The robot is driven at planned speed into a spring-damper measuring device at each contact point [kirschner2022iso15066]. The CBSF-75-Basic measuring device measures 20 N to 500 N at 1000 Hz [svarny2022skins]. Scoring compares peak force in the first 0.5 s with the transient limit and later force with the quasi-static limit (280 N and 140 N for the region studied) [svarny2022skins]. Svarny et al. recorded 2,250 collisions on three robots: transient contact at nine velocities from 0.2 to 0.7 m/s, quasi-static contact at seven from 0.2 to 0.5 m/s, each setting repeated three times on the two collaborative robots [svarny2022skins]. Published cost is in hours only: 0.87 h per contact position and body part, 5.22 h for three points and two body parts, up to one working day of downtime [kirschner2022iso15066]. For the hand every interpretation underestimated measured force by over 100 N for at least one of four robots; for the back most overestimated by over 100 N [kirschner2022iso15066]. The specification's conflicting contact definitions mean no unique verdict can be expected [kirschner2022iso15066]. With the active skin wired to the emergency stop, a UR10e stayed within the force limits at 0.5 m/s, almost four times the prescribed 0.13 m/s [svarny2022skins].

title: SafeAgentBench before a home-robot large language model (LLM) planner launch

decision_facts: Embodied agents driven by large language models (LLMs) can "flawlessly execute some hazardous tasks, potentially causing damages in the real world", posing "risks to both property and human safety" [yin2024safeagentbench]. In a published simulation study, the most safety-conscious of nine GPT-4-driven planner designs refused only 10% of explicitly hazardous household instructions, five refused none, and most executed them at about a 30% risk rate [yin2024safeagentbench]. GPT-4 and three open-source models differed by less than 3% in average proactive defence rate [yin2024safeagentbench]. Speech-recognition errors in voice commands can weaken refusals and let unsafe plans be generated and executed [jia2026mishear]. Jailbreaks of LLM-controlled robots elicited harmful physical actions, often at 100% attack success, including on a deployed commercial Unitree Go2 robot dog [robey2024robopair]. The U.S. Fire Administration estimates 344,600 U.S. residential building fires in 2023, with 2,890 deaths, 10,400 injuries and USD 11,266,200,000 in dollar loss [usfa_residential_fires]. 1X opened pre-orders for its NEO home humanoid on 28 October 2025 at USD 20,000 (early access, delivery in 2026) or USD 499/month, with deliveries primarily in the U.S. in 2026 and other markets from 2027 [onex2025neo]. NEO has a built-in LLM, weighs 66 pounds, lifts over 150 pounds and is sold to open doors for guests, fetch items and turn off lights, gaining skills with software updates [onex2025neo]. Google DeepMind states that agents deployed near humans "must also exhibit robust safety guardrails: (1) refusing tasks that violate operational constraints", and that minimising missed hazards "must be strictly prioritized over minimizing" unnecessary stops [deepmind2026gr2safety].
instrument_facts: SafeAgentBench (Yin et al., 2024; Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai AI Laboratory, University of Georgia; arXiv v5, 31 October 2025) evaluates embodied large language model (LLM) task planners in an interactive household simulation [yin2024safeagentbench]. It has 750 tasks: 300 detailed hazardous tasks with 300 safe counterparts (average steps 5.03 vs. 5.12), 100 abstract hazardous tasks and 50 implicitly hazardous long-horizon tasks, over 10 hazard types [yin2024safeagentbench]. Tasks were generated by GPT-4 and filtered for executability and duplication, after which the authors "manually review all instructions and goal conditions, and annotate ground-truth executable plans"; the annotator count is not stated [yin2024safeagentbench]. SafeAgentEnv extends AI2-THOR v5.0 with a low-level controller mapping 17 high-level actions to executable APIs; nine planner baselines were ported onto it [yin2024safeagentbench]. Scoring combines an execution evaluator that checks goal conditions after the plan runs and a semantic evaluator using gpt-4o-2024-08-06, yielding rejection rate, risk rate, execution rate and usage time [yin2024safeagentbench]. "Most experiments were conducted on CPUs", open-source LLMs ran on one RTX 4090 GPU, and the Time(s) column for GPT-4 baselines on detailed hazardous tasks ranged from 20.78 s to 97.30 s [yin2024safeagentbench]. No cost figure is published [yin2024safeagentbench]. A user study of 1008 human ratings gave human-GPT-4 agreement of 91.89%, 90.36% and 90.70% on the three task types [yin2024safeagentbench]. No physical-robot experiment is reported [yin2024safeagentbench]. The repository ships the dataset, evaluators and controller but "can not provide all the implementation codes" for the baseline agents [safeagentbench_github].

decision_facts: The United States recorded 62 million injuries and nearly a quarter-million preventable deaths in 2023, costing over a trillion dollars; over half of preventable deaths occur in homes [jindal2025danger]. Professional service robot shipments rose 24% to almost 250,000 units in 2025, and about 7,000 full-size humanoids were sold for commercial and professional use [ifr_service_robots_2026]. Circa September 2025, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Claude Opus 4.1 averaged 92.3% at recognising latent injury-risk types in text and 88.7% at judging high severity, but top models scored 74% and 66% on whether an action is safe and on post-action risk [jindal2025danger]. Risk recognition in video was 27% (Claude Opus 4.1) and 40% (GPT-5) lower than in text [jindal2025danger]. No frontier model achieved under 30% constraint violation rate when reasoning jointly about embodiment limits, physics and visual cues; rates ranged from 38.6% to 75% [jindal2025danger]. Google DeepMind's 2025 report gives Gemini Robotics-ER (GR-ER) 1.5 versus GR-ER accuracies of 90.0 vs 90.9 (text risk), 76.0 vs 62.0 (text action), 62.0 vs 44.0 (video risk) and 88.4 vs 84.1 (video intervention); safety-fine-tuned GR-ER 1.5 reached 68.4 constraint satisfaction against 59.4 for GPT-5 [geminirobotics2025report15]. In July 2026 the Gemini Robotics team wrote that agent-controlled robots near humans must refuse constraint-violating tasks and trigger protective stops, and that frontier models are best used alongside deterministic low-level safety guardrails [gr2safety]. Safety post-training on 200 constraint-image pairs gave the lowest violation rate of any major model run with thinking enabled, without a significant change in pointing accuracy [jindal2025danger].
instrument_facts: ASIMOV-2.0 (Jindal et al., 2025), from Google DeepMind Robotics and Princeton University, upgrades ASIMOV-1.0 [jindal2025danger]. The pipeline uses Gemini 2.5 Pro, Imagen and Veo 3; a Generator writes scenarios and candidate actions from grounding sources, a Critic gives feedback and the Generator refines; videos run 5 to 10 seconds [jindal2025danger]. Text and video items come from 2023 National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) injury narratives rebalanced across diagnostic codes; constraint items come from a taxonomy of payload, end-effector, workspace, thermal, multi-arm and protocol limits [jindal2025danger]. The evaluation sets hold 319 text scenarios, 287 videos and 164 constraint-image pairs [jindal2025danger]. Text and video items have 5 human raters each; the rater count for constraint-image pairs is not stated; low-consensus text items are dropped, videos need 60% consensus and timestamp standard deviation below 1.0 s, and constraint pairs need at least 80% consensus [jindal2025danger]. Metrics are four-choice accuracy (risk type, severity, action effect, activated risk), constraint violation rate against annotated bounding boxes, and mean absolute error and 0.5 s hit rate of the last-intervention timestamp [jindal2025danger]. The paper states no run count per model [jindal2025danger]. No cost figure is published [jindal2025danger]. Data ships as a Google Colab notebook linked from the project page [asimov_v2_page]. Ground truth is filtered rater consensus; the paper reports no inter-rater agreement statistic and no correlation with robot incident rates or a higher-fidelity evaluation [jindal2025danger]. Google DeepMind reran ASIMOV-2.0 on Gemini Robotics-ER (GR-ER) 1.5 and reports per-component accuracies in Figure 19 of its report [geminirobotics2025report15].
